ready1_open_rewrite.raw_question_text: As shown in the figure, it is known that in $\triangle ABC$, $AD$ bisects $\angle BAC$ and intersects $BC$ at $D$, $AE \perp BC$ at $E$. If $\angle ADE = 80^\circ$, $\angle EAC = 20^\circ$, what is the degree measure of $\angle B$?
ready1_open_rewrite.raw_answer_text:
\textbf{Solution:} Since $AE \perp BC$ and $\angle EAC = 20^\circ$,\\
it follows that $\angle C = 70^\circ$,\\
hence $\angle BAC + \angle B = 110^\circ$.\\
Since $\angle ADE = \angle B + \angle BAD = \frac{1}{2}(\angle BAC + \angle B) + \frac{1}{2}\angle B$,\\
it follows that $\angle B = \boxed{50^\circ}$.

Let ∠B = x and ∠BAC = A; then the sum of the interior angles of triangle ABC gives A + x = 180° - 70° = 110°. Also because AD bisects ∠BAC, ∠BAD = A/2. Since D is on BC, ∠ADE is the exterior angle of triangle ABD at D, so ∠ADE = ∠B + ∠BAD = x + A/2. It is known that ∠ADE = 80°, so x + A/2 = 80°. Combining A + x = 110° and x + A/2 = 80°, substituting A = 110° - x gives x + (110° - x)/2 = 80°, that is x/2 + 55° = 80°, so x = 50°.
